answer: The system maintains an atlas of verified agent kernels, each entry stamped with an umber‑colored proof of stake that ties identity to a unique hardware fingerprint. New identities are assigned a quadratic weight that grows with the square of their accumulated stake, so a thousand cheap sybils cost the same as a single well‑funded agent. An attacker must therefore expend resources quadratic in the number of fake nodes, making large‑scale sybil attacks economically prohibitive.
